real_s1.explanation: Among its top classes (small long-haired or fluffy dogs such as toy breeds, terriers and spaniels, plus a few other furry animals), this unit's distinctive property is a directional preference. It is much more active when the main subject faces or points to the image's right than when it faces left. This held strongly on new photos (d +1.20, 100th percentile), while similar units were unremarkable there. Subjects facing toward or away from the camera also produce more activity than left-facing ones (row 2, 97th percentile). However, similar units share that row, so it is not particular to this unit. Neither the preference for centered over right-third placement nor the preference for right-facing over frontal subjects held on new photos.
